notes: Percent conventions: where the game treats a stat as a multiplier on a 100% base (Luck, Greed, Might), values are stored as fractional deltas (e.g. +10% -> 0.10) in *Bonus fields, and as explicit multipliers only where a source states a multiplier (e.g. maxHealth PowerUp multiplierPerRank 1.1). All times in seconds. sources.note: Community mirror (github.com/SurvivatonsAndMore/VampireSurvivorsFiles) of the game's shipped JSON data files, game version 1.16. Files used: PowerUp.json, Item.json, Stage.json, Props.json. Base-game folder; DLC content lives in sibling folders. Entries additionally carry a contentGroup field ('BASE' vs 'EXTRA') used below to flag non-base-game content.

conflicts.note: One source gives per-chest-level gold bands; the other gives a single 60-500 range for any chest. The per-level bands are the more recent/likely-current figures but this was not verifiable without direct page access.

7,818,959 (base 1,911,240 + fees 5,907,719) vs 27,148,513 (base 2,469,640 + fees 24,678,873). Almost certainly different game versions / different PowerUp counts. Use the official-wiki figure for a current base-game reference. RE-CHECKED against shipped data v1.16: computing the documented formula over all 29 PowerUps / 125 total ranks gives base 1,362,240 + fees 29,861,494 = 31,223,734. This does not match either wiki figure, which is expected - the wiki pages describe earlier versions with fewer PowerUps and ranks. Note the shipped BASE total (1,362,240) is LOWER than both wiki base figures while the fee total is far higher, consistent with the fee term compounding over a larger rank count (125). Use 31,223,734 for v1.16.
27 is stated to include the separate Seal PowerUps.

Wiki states Luck raises the weight of every light-source drop except Gold Coin and Coin Bag, which would include Little Clover. Shipped Item.json flags isRare:true (the 'Drop rate affected by Luck' tooltip) on only ROAST, OROLOGION, VACUUM, COINBAGMAX, ROSARY, NFT and SORBETTO - NOT on CLOVER, GILDED or PICKUP_REROLL_DICE. floorPickups.notes: All of these drop from destroyed light sources unless stated otherwise. 'Rarity' on the wiki is the relative weight of the item in the light-source loot pool; Luck multiplies that weight for everything except Gold Coin and Coin Bag. Exact weight values were not retrievable. Drop weights, level gates and Luck flags below are now taken from the shipped Item.json (v1.16). Two further BASE light-source pickups not in the original brief exist: Gilded Clover (weight 1, unlocks at character level 30) and, with Arcana XII, Sorbetto (weight 1, contentGroup EXTRA). See data.lightSources.dropTable for the full pool.

luckRules.mechanism: Luck multiplies the weight ('rarity') of every pickup in the light-source pool EXCEPT Gold Coin and Coin Bag, so it shifts the distribution toward rare drops.
luckRules.spawnCapCaveat: While the maximum number of light sources is already on the map, spawn attempts are no longer influenced by Luck, so they spawn less often.
luckRules.shippedDataMechanism: Item.json flags entries with isRare:true; these are exactly the ones whose tooltip reads 'Drop rate affected by Luck.' Luck multiplies the weight of isRare entries only.

lightSources.stageNotes: Most DLC stages, and Capella Magna, have a higher maximum light-source count than standard base-game stages. Exact per-stage numbers not retrieved.
lightSources.dropTableNotes: 'rarityWeight' is the raw weight from Item.json. A destroyed light source picks ONE entry weighted by rarityWeight, restricted to entries whose unlocksAtCharacterLevel the player has reached (and whose requiresArcana/requiresItem conditions are met). 'baseShareAtZeroLuck' is weight / total-BASE-weight assuming every base entry is eligible and Luck is at base - it is a derived convenience value, not a shipped number, and the real share is higher for early-game pickups because level-gated entries are absent from the pool.

propTypes.note: Props.json lists the destructible art/HP definitions only; it carries no drop table.

fields.maxDestructibles: maximum light sources alive on the map at once

treasureChests.rollOrder: The game checks each treasure level starting from level 3 (5 items), falling through to level 2 (3 items), then level 1 (1 item). If all checks fail, the chest's base level is used.

variables.levelChance: the per-level probability configured on the specific boss/enemy that dropped the chest
variables.totalLuck: displayed Luck percentage + 100, expressed as a multiplier (e.g. +30% Luck -> 1.30)

luckFormula.note: Per-level base chances are configured individually per boss enemy, so there is no single global table.

exampleBaseOdds.enemy: Silver Bat (first one in Mad Forest at 9:00)
exampleBaseOdds.note: Rolled in that order; each roll is multiplied by totalLuck. CONFIRMED against shipped data v1.16: Stage.json FOREST minute 9 treasure.chances == [3,10,50].

treasureChests.rollTiming: Chest contents/level are determined when the chest is OPENED, not when it drops. Leaving chests on the ground until Luck is higher works.

evolutionRules.note: When evolution/union requirements are met and the run is at 10:00 or later, chests can evolve or unite a weapon. Generally only one weapon evolves per chest, including higher-tier chests, though some chests contain multiple evolutions.

treasureChests.fallbackReward: If nothing in the player's inventory can be upgraded, chests award extra coins instead.

baseOddsPerBoss.structureNote: CORRECTION to the wiki framing: the chest configuration is attached to each STAGE-MINUTE entry in Stage.json (field 'treasure'), not to the enemy/boss itself. Each entry has chances:[a,b,c] = the raw percent chances for the 5-item, 3-item and 1-item rolls respectively, checked in that order with fallthrough, plus 'level' = the chest's base level used if all three rolls fail, and prizeTypes/fixedPrizes describing what the slots contain. Chances below are converted to fractions (30 -> 0.30). Each is multiplied by totalLuck at open time.
baseOddsPerBoss.verification: Mad Forest minute 9 (boss BAT5, the Silver Bat) reads chances [3,10,50] in shipped data, exactly matching the wiki's documented 3%/10%/50% example. The wiki example is confirmed.

inRunSources: Gold Coin pickups from light sources (1 gold x Greed)
Coin Bag from light sources (10 gold x Greed)
Rich Coin Bag from light sources after level 5 (100 gold x Greed)

Extra coins from chests / level-ups when nothing can be upgraded

greed.displayConvention: The stat panel shows the DIFFERENCE from base Greed; +30% displayed means 130% total Greed (multiplier 1.30).
greed.stacking: Character bonuses, PowerUps and items stack ADDITIVELY into the Greed total. Stage-level gold bonuses stack MULTIPLICATIVELY with that collective total.

maxKnownCombo.note: The Bone Zone in Hyper mode doubles overall gold gain; combined with +100% Greed this gives 4x base gold.

endOfRunPayout.note: Stated as an additional reward on death/run end after completing the stage, +100 per revival left unused. Gold gathered in-run persists to the account whether the run ends in death or completion. Whether the 500 applies to all base-game stages or only to stage completion specifically was not verifiable.

powerUpShop.powerUpCountNote: 29 distinct PowerUp entries in shipped data v1.16 (counting Seal I-IV separately). Official wiki says 27, Fandom says 24 - those are older game versions and/or exclude the four Seals and the later-update additions (Omni, Charm, Defang, Recycle, Antipiretic, Invul Time). A strict launch-era base game is a smaller set; the scope flag is kept deliberately.

variables.bought: ranks of THIS PowerUp already bought
variables.totalBought: ranks of ALL PowerUps already bought (drives the global fee)

costFormula.baseCostRule: Each rank bought raises the base cost of the next rank of the same PowerUp by initialPrice. E.g. initialPrice 200 -> 5 ranks cost 200+400+600+800+1000 = 3000 in base cost, before fees.
costFormula.feeRule: The fee term floor(20 * 1.1^totalBought) is a GLOBAL fee driven by the total number of ranks bought across all PowerUps. No fee is applied while totalBought == 0. Since v0.7.2 (9 June 2022) fees are additive, so purchase order no longer affects the total.

powerUpShop.disableRule: After maxing a PowerUp the player may disable it, except for Rerolls, Skips, Banishes and Seals.

powerUpShop.totalCostNote: Derived from shipped data v1.16 using the documented cost formula, buying every rank of all 29 PowerUps. Differs from both wiki figures because v1.16 contains more PowerUps and more ranks than the versions those pages describe.
powerUpShop.perRankCostOrderNote: BASE cost per rank is order-INDEPENDENT: rank i of a PowerUp always costs initialPrice*i. Only the global FEE term is order-dependent in WHICH purchase it lands on, but because the fee depends solely on totalBought (ranks bought so far across all PowerUps) and is additive since v0.7.2, the SUM of fees over a full clear is also order-independent. Therefore the per-rank base table below plus the fee schedule fully determine any purchase order's cost; no assumed order is required for the total.

overview.unlockSystem: Collecting the Randomazzo relic in Gallo Tower unlocks the Arcana system and the first Arcana, Sarabande of Healing (VI). The remaining base-set Arcanas are unlocked either by reaching level 50 with certain characters, or by surviving to the 31:00 mark on certain stages.
overview.selection: Arcanas can be toggled on/off from the stage-select screen. With Arcanas enabled, the player normally obtains up to three per run: one is chosen from any unlocked Arcana at the start of the run, and the others are offered at set points during the run. Certain effects allow obtaining more than three.
overview.extraSet: Collecting the Darkasso in Room 1665 unlocks a further 'Darkana' set, unlocked by tasks with other characters.
overview.theme: Loosely based on the real-world Major Arcana tarot deck.
